units.titleZh: 數字與時間 × 語言與句型

passages.title: Numbers and Time: First Reading
passages.text: At eleven a.m., our English teacher gives us a new word. We read it together and ask what it is about. Ben knows where it is in the book, but he does not know why it is there. After an hour, we can say the word and write it. Every child feels great because what we say is true. We will study together every afternoon.

passages.title: Language Tools: Second Reading
passages.text: Two hours ago, Amy called me after school. She wanted help with three English words, so she walked to my home. We read the words with my sister in the afternoon. When the sun was down, Amy asked where she could put her book. I put her book in a bag. In the evening, she walked home and said, "I know every word now." I said, "Great!" because it was true.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: When can we study our English words together?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: How about eleven a.m. after breakfast?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I have school then. Is the afternoon OK?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. Where do you want to study?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: At my house, with my sister.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Great. We can study for one hour.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Why do you need these word cards?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Because I read them every evening.

units.titleZh: 人物與家庭 × 數字與時間
units.titleEn: People and Family & Numbers and Time

passages.title: People and Family: First Reading
passages.text: Yesterday morning, my aunt and uncle came to our house at eight o'clock. Dad made breakfast, and every child helped. My brother gave the children milk, and I put food on the table. My uncle is a worker, so he had to go at eleven a.m. Before he went, Daddy took a family picture. We said good-bye and asked him to come again in one week.

passages.title: Numbers and Time: Second Reading
passages.text: Our school family day started at two p.m. yesterday. My friend Ben came with his dad, aunt, and two children. His daddy helped the teacher, and my family made drinks. At three o'clock, the children started to run. Ben was slow, but his friend helped him. They tried to run together. Every child said their run was great, even with zero prizes.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: When does our family breakfast start tomorrow?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It starts at eight o'clock in the morning.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Will Aunt Anna and Uncle Ben come?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, they will come with their children.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Can I invite my friend Sam too?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, his dad can come after work.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Great, I will call him before two p.m.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Please help Daddy put the food on the table.

units.titleZh: 動物與自然 × 身體與感受
units.titleEn: Animals and Nature & Body and Feelings

passages.title: Animals and Nature: First Reading
passages.text: The weather was hot when our teacher took us to the zoo. I saw a big elephant take food with its nose. A child asked why the animal had no hair on its body. A duck put its head down and sat under a tree. I put my hand in my bag and found an apple. I was hungry, so I ate it with my lunch.

passages.title: Body and Feelings: Second Reading
passages.text: Ben and I went to the sea with a kite. The weather was fine, so Ben started to run. The kite went up, but it came down into a tree. Ben was sad and put his head on my arm. I asked him to help me. He took my hand, and we got it down together. The kite was fine. A star was in the evening sky when we walked home.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Why is that duck under the tree?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It may feel hot in this weather.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Can we give the animal some water?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, put the cup by its head.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: My hand is dirty from the chalk.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Your bag has water. Please wash it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: After that, can we fly my kite?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, we can fly it this evening.

units.titleZh: 食物與用餐 × 校園與學習
units.titleEn: Food and Meals & School and Learning

passages.title: Food and Meals: First Reading
passages.text: Before school, Mia ate a banana and drank milk for breakfast. In the classroom, the teacher asked the children to write about their food. Mia had a computer, but she could not spell banana. She asked a friend and then wrote the word. Her eraser fell under the desk. She found it with an old cookie under the desk. The teacher said, "Please do not eat cookies in the classroom."

passages.title: School and Learning: Second Reading
passages.text: Dad and I made beef and rice for dinner. My sister made cold drinks with juice and ice. She gave me a cookie, but I wanted it after dinner. While Dad made the food, I used the computer to learn a new English word. I wrote it on a card and asked my sister to spell it. She spelled it well, so I gave her two cookies after we ate.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What did you eat for breakfast today?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I ate a banana and two cookies.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Did you make the cookies at school?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, we read about them on a computer.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Did you write how to make them?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, but I could not spell banana.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Did your teacher give you an eraser?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, then each child ate one cookie.

units.titleZh: 食物與用餐 × 住家與物品
units.titleEn: Food and Meals & Home and Objects

passages.title: Food and Meals: First Reading
passages.text: It was hot after school, so Amy came to my house. We went into the kitchen and made ice cream with milk and ice. I put in too much salt, but Amy said it was still good. We took the ice cream and juice to the dining room. Dad came home with hot dogs for dinner. We ate together and gave him a big cup of ice cream.

passages.title: Clothes and Looks: Second Reading
passages.text: Mia wanted to wear her new dress to a family dinner. The weather was cold, so her aunt gave her a coat and a red hat. Before they left the house, the telephone rang in the dining room. Her uncle was on the phone. He asked Mia to call him on her phone when they got there. Mia said yes, put on her coat, and walked out with her aunt.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Why are you wearing that coat and hat?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We are eating dinner at my aunt's house.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Are you wearing your new red dress?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, but the weather is very cold.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Should I bring some juice?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Bring juice, because we have hot dogs.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good, I will call her on my phone.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Great, please come before dinner starts.

units.titleZh: 地點與交通 × 動作與日常
units.titleEn: Places and Transport & Actions and Routines

passages.title: Places and Transport: First Reading
passages.text: My friend Sam came from America for a family trip. Dad did not drive because we wanted to take a train to the sea. On the train, Sam saw a bird fly in the sky. When we got there, we saw a big truck at a store. Dad called his friend, and the man gave us two bicycles. We had a great afternoon on the bikes.

passages.title: Actions and Routines: Second Reading
passages.text: Emma wanted to try her new bicycle after school. Dad helped her get on the bike, and she started to go. A truck came by, so Dad asked her to wait. When it was gone, Emma tried again. She went too fast, and her bike went into a tree. She did not cry because her arm and leg were fine. Dad called home and said, "Emma can go now!"

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Are we taking the train for our trip?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, Dad does not want to drive.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Can we take our bikes with us?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No, but Uncle Sam has two bicycles.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Should I call him and ask now?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, he came back from America yesterday.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Look, a red kite can fly very high.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Great, we can take it on our trip.

passages.title: Actions and Routines: First Reading
passages.text: In autumn, our school asked families to join a dance. I invited my friend Lily because she wanted to try it. We needed two hats, so we made them with old cards. Lily helped me, and we waited for the glue to dry. At school, the teacher asked us to dance together. We tried three times. After the dance, I took the hats home.

passages.title: Actions and Routines: Second Reading
passages.text: Dad came home from work and said he needed help. Our dog was dirty after a walk, so we had to wash and dry it. I took water, and Dad made a warm bed. The dog tried to run, but Dad asked it to wait. When its hair was dry, I kissed its head. The dog went to sleep, and Dad said we did great work.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Do you want to join our ball game?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, but I need help kicking the ball.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Try again, and kick the ball slowly.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Okay, please wait while I take my coat.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Your coat is still wet from the rain.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I will put it here to dry.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good. We can make two teams together.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Great, I will invite Lily after school.

passages.title: Everyday English: First Reading
passages.text: At school, we made a store with toys and books. I had ten dollars in play money. I looked down and saw a car under the table. "Oops, is there any money with it?" I asked. Ben said, "Uh-uh, but the car is one dollar." I really wanted it, so I gave him one dollar. Then we put everything up and said good-bye.

passages.title: Everyday English: Second Reading
passages.text: Emma and I were singing together in her room. Her baby brother was sleeping, so we had to sing slowly. Then Emma stood up, but I looked down at the words. "Oh-oh, I do not know this word," I said. Emma said it with me, and I could sing again. Her brother opened his eyes. "Oops!" we said, and we gave him a toy.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Do you have any money with you?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Uh-uh, I only have one dollar.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Really? Your bag is down there.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Oops, my money is in that bag.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good, but our bus is here now.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let us take the bag together.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay, I have it. Good-bye, Amy.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Goodbye, Ben. See you at school.
